title: 狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居与柜子里的深海巨怪
pdf: https://michael-podcast-1513696684.cos.ap-chengdu.myqcloud.com/vol09/Vol09_晚读讲义_狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居与柜子里的深海巨怪_v1.pdf
pdfName: Vol09_晚读讲义_狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居与柜子里的深海巨怪_v1.pdf

blocks.en: Hello, young explorers, and welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! Today, both of our stars are champions of hide-and-seek. One hid in a museum for almost a hundred years. The other hid in front of everybody's eyes for forty years. Nobody had to find them in the wild. Somebody just had to look at them.
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 欢迎回来，小小探险家们，这里是 Michael 的早听晚读！今天的两位主角都是捉迷藏冠军：一位在博物馆里躲了近一百年，另一位在所有人的眼皮底下躲了四十年。没人需要去野外寻找它们——只要有人仔仔细细地看它们一眼就好。

blocks.en: Our first story begins in Egypt, beside the famous Sphinx. The Great Sphinx of Giza, lion-bodied and king-faced, was carved from a ridge of limestone, rock that was once a warm sea floor. Inside those rocks, scientists have recognised a crocodile never named before.
blocks.title: 狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居
blocks.cn: 我们的第一个故事发生在埃及，就在著名的狮身人面像身旁。吉萨的大狮身人面像，狮子的身体、国王的面孔，是从一整片石灰岩山脊上雕刻出来的——而这片岩石，曾经是一片温暖浅海的海底。就在这片岩石里，科学家认出了一只从未被命名过的鳄鱼。

blocks.en: The animal, Herugavialis cairensis, lived forty-five million years ago. It was a gavial, a crocodile with a long, thin snout for snapping up fish, and a curved ridge circled each of its eyes.
blocks.title: 狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居
blocks.cn: 这只动物名叫 Herugavialis cairensis（赫鲁长吻鳄），生活在四千五百万年前。它是一种长吻鳄，有着又长又细的嘴，专门用来抓鱼；它的每只眼睛周围，都环绕着一圈弯弯的隆起。

blocks.en: Our hero is a skull. Collectors dug it out of the Mokattam rocks in the nineteen twenties. It travelled to a German museum and slept for almost a hundred years. Its label named a known crocodile, and nobody questioned it for decades.
blocks.title: 狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居
blocks.cn: 我们的主角是一颗头骨。二十世纪二十年代，收藏家们从莫卡塔姆岩石群里把它挖了出来。它被送到德国的一家博物馆，一睡就是近一百年。它的标签上写着一种已知鳄鱼的名字，几十年来，从没有人怀疑过。

blocks.en: Then an international team took a closer look. They slid the skull into a CT scanner, a machine that lets doctors and scientists peek inside objects without breaking them open. After comparing three hundred details, the team concluded: this was not the crocodile on the label. It was a new genus, a branch that science had missed.
blocks.title: 狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居
blocks.cn: 后来，一个国际团队决定认真看一看。他们把头骨滑进一台 CT 扫描仪——这种机器能让医生和科学家在不打破物体的情况下看清它的内部。在比较了三百处细节之后，团队得出结论：这根本不是标签上的那种鳄鱼。这是一个全新的“属”，是鳄鱼家族树上一条被科学漏掉的枝杈。

blocks.en: They named it after Heru, a god linked with the Sphinx. And like the Sphinx, it is missing the tip of its snout.
blocks.title: 狮身人面像的鳄鱼邻居
blocks.cn: 团队用 Heru 为它命名，那是一位与狮身人面像有关的古埃及神。而且和狮身人面像一样，它也缺了鼻尖。

blocks.en: Our second treasure was hiding in plain sight in a university collection in Germany. It looks like a woodlouse that swallowed a growth potion: hard scaly shell, many legs. It is a giant isopod, a deep-sea cousin of the tiny pill bugs, only this one is thirty-two centimetres long. Scientists call monsters this size colossogiants.
blocks.title: 柜子里的深海巨怪
blocks.cn: 我们的第二件宝贝同样藏在眼皮底下，这次是在德国一所大学的收藏室里。它看起来像一只吞了长大药水的潮虫：硬硬的鳞片壳、许多条腿。它是一只巨型等足虫，是小小潮虫的深海亲戚，只不过这一只长达三十二厘米。科学家把这个尺寸的怪兽叫作 colossogiants（巨无霸级）。

blocks.en: It came from the Caribbean Sea, near Puerto Rico, caught in a seabed trap five hundred metres down. Giant isopods patrol the dark ocean floor, down to two thousand five hundred metres, eating whatever sinks: fish, squid, even whales. These armoured cleaners help digest the ocean’s leftovers.
blocks.title: 柜子里的深海巨怪
blocks.cn: 它来自波多黎各附近的加勒比海，在五百米深的海床陷阱里被捕获。巨型等足虫在黑暗的深海海底巡逻，最深可达两千五百米，吃一切沉下来的东西：鱼、乌贼，甚至鲸鱼。这些身披铠甲的清洁工，帮忙消化海洋的剩饭剩菜。

blocks.en: For forty years, its label used a cousin’s name. It even starred in a sea-giants exhibition. Everyone saw it; nobody saw it.
blocks.title: 柜子里的深海巨怪
blocks.cn: 四十年来，它的标签一直用着一个亲戚的名字。它甚至还在一场“海洋巨兽”展览里当过明星。所有人都看见了它，却没有人真正看见它。

blocks.en: Then a researcher and the curator wheeled it into an X-ray scanner. The scans, with tiny details of mouth and shell, proved it was a new species. Its closest relative lives near Mexico’s Yucatán coast. Its name joins its two homes: its birth island, and the town of its recognition.
blocks.title: 柜子里的深海巨怪
blocks.cn: 后来，一位研究者和收藏负责人把它推进了一台 X 光扫描仪。扫描结果，再加上它嘴巴和外壳上的细微之处，证明了这是一个新物种。它最近的亲戚生活在墨西哥尤卡坦海岸附近。它的名字把它的两个“家”连在一起：它出生的岛，和它最终被认出的小镇。

blocks.en: You need no ship or submarine to find a new species. Sometimes it sits on a shelf, hiding in plain sight, waiting for someone to look twice.
blocks.title: 柜子里的深海巨怪
blocks.cn: 寻找新物种，不需要轮船，也不需要潜水艇。有时它就坐在一只架子上，藏在眼皮底下，等着有人愿意多看它一眼。

blocks.en: Here’s today’s idiom: "hiding in plain sight." If something is hiding in plain sight, everyone can see it, but nobody notices it — like a new species sitting on a museum shelf for forty years! Here’s an example: "The keys were hiding in plain sight, on the kitchen table." What treasure might be hiding in plain sight in your home?
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是：“hiding in plain sight”（藏在眼皮底下）。如果一样东西 hiding in plain sight，那就是所有人都能看见它，却偏偏没人注意到它——就像一个新物种在博物馆的架子上坐了四十年！举个例子：“钥匙就藏在眼皮底下，在厨房的桌子上。”你家里会有什么宝贝，正藏在眼皮底下呢？

blocks.en: Let's think about today's stories. A crocodile hid in a museum for a hundred years, and a sea giant for forty. Now, two questions for you. First: if you could peek inside one museum drawer, what would you hope to find? Second: what thing in your home deserves a second look? Talk about it with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 我们来想想今天的故事。一只鳄鱼在博物馆里躲了一百年，一只深海巨兽躲了四十年。现在轮到你回答两个问题。第一：如果你能偷看一眼博物馆的某个抽屉，你希望在里面找到什么？第二：你家里有哪件东西，值得你再仔细看上一眼？和家人聊聊吧！

blocks.en: That's all for today, young explorers. Keep your eyes open, look twice — a treasure may be hiding in plain sight! See you tomorrow morning!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，小小探险家们。睁大眼睛，多看两眼——说不定一件宝贝就藏在你的眼皮底下！明天早上见！

quiz.title: B. 单项选择（Single Choice）
questions:
Where did the crocodile skull sleep for almost a hundred years?
A. In a pyramid in Egypt
B. In a museum in Germany
C. In a university in Mexico
D. Inside the Great Sphinx

What did both teams use to look inside their specimens?
A. A CT scanner or an X-ray scanner
B. A submarine camera
C. A time machine
D. A magnifying glass

How deep under the sea was the giant isopod caught?
A. Five thousand metres
B. Fifty metres
C. Five hundred metres
D. Twenty-five metres

What does "hiding in plain sight" mean?
A. Hidden in a place nobody can reach
B. In a place everyone can see, but nobody notices
C. Deep under the sea
D. Locked inside a dark box

children.text: that lets doctors and scientists peek
They slid the skull into a CT scanner.
（他们把头骨滑进了一台 CT 扫描仪）主语
交代方向。先抓住主干，后面再长也不怕。
指的是同一个东西，换个说法再解释一遍——“一台机器”。同位语就像给名词配的一张小名片，读到它，陌生名词立刻变亲切。
that lets doctors and scientists peek inside objects
在从句里作主语（指机器），所以
——这一点和作宾语时可以省略正好相反，要分清。
let + 宾语 + 动词原形
的固定用法：let somebody do something。
结构，表示“在不……的情况下”：不用把物体打破，就能看清内部。它的动作发出者，就是前面的
放进扫描仪（动作）→ 它是一台机器（同位语解释）→ 能让人看进内部（定语从句说功能）→ 而且不用打破（without 短语说方式）
。一句话，把一台神奇机器讲得明明白白。
"travelled to a German museum and slept for almost a hundred years."
, and the isopod was wheeled into
— both teams peeked inside with scanners.
"caught in a seabed trap five hundred metres down."
(The deepest isopods patrol down to two thousand five hundred metres — a different number!)
